convoLines.text: «¡Hola! ¿Cómo te llamas?»
They answer at length. They nod back, slowly.
They answer at length. They smile back, slower this time, like it just landed.
They answer at length. You press a hand to your own chest, then point at them. Together — they get it.
A final shared look — you both feel the talk running its course.
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.
"I'm sorry — I'm feverish, a cut gone hot and angry. Can you do anything?"
"The cut's gone hot and it's spreading — I can feel it moving. Clean it out, wrap it tight, please. Before it turns."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"This one — Wild Ginger. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"Grayson is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Sleep's gone strange. I hum one note, over and over, when the dark comes at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Lillian grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Lillian is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"The fire feels smaller without Grayson. The rest of us will have to be bigger."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"I hate to ask this, but I'm feverish, a cut gone hot and angry. Will you help me?"
"It's not just the cut anymore, it's in the blood, I can feel it climbing. I need someone who knows wounds."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Grayson always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
You show them Black Walnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"...I need to go be quiet for a while."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"This wound — I can't clean it properly one-handed. Could you clean it out for me? Please."
"It keeps getting worse. I can't haul or hunt with it like this — and if it festers, I'm done for. Please, clean it out and bind it tight."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
They go very still. Not relaxed-still. Held-still.
"Ha." Not amused. "So you figured it out. Yeah, I took 1× Stone. What are you going to do about it?"
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
Something eases in their shoulders. They're really talking to you now.
"...Okay. I'll figure it out." They won't ask twice. That much is clear.
"Still on that wound care."
"We went over this," Lorenzo says, a little tired. "I already told you the truth about that."
"Right. Go on, then."
"Okay. I'll manage on my own."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About this wound — I still haven't found anyone. Any chance?"
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Lillian is gone and Owen is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"I keep turning over the last thing Owen said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Lillian nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"We bury, we grieve, we keep going. There's no step four."
"Still on what's been happening."
You show them Black Walnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Well. My social battery is officially dead."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can we talk?" Omar shifts their weight. "I need something to do. Anything. Please."
"About this wound — the need hasn't gone anywhere. I'm still asking."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Last time things were different. They always are." "Lorenzo always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Omar is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Like I said — Still on what's been happening."
"Where are you from — originally? Before all this."
"Okay." Something shutters, just slightly.
"Right. Go on, then."
"No — you're right, it's a lot. Forget it."
"This was good." They mean it.
They speak. You understand none of it. "Fuck you." — they grin, proud of the one English they know.
They answer at length. They nod back, a little quicker this time.
They answer at length. A smile, tired but real.
They answer at length. You point at yourself, then at them, then at the fire. Together. They get it.
They glance toward their own thoughts; the exchange is winding down.
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.

lines: d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Grayson Boyd is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d41: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d41: 🕯️ Grayson Boyd is dead — the expedition. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d41: What Grayson kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d41: "Grayson's gone." Lillian looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Grayson." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d41: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Stan blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Tainted Bait (Level 1). Your bait is tainted — traps catch 50% more. (The poison’s in the bait, not your hands. Mostly.)
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Animal Behavior (Level 1). Most animals flee. Give them an escape route and they take it. Cornered animals fight.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Wire Snares (Level 1). A loop of wire on a game trail. Simple, effective, ancient. Check at dawn.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Tripwire (Level 1). You string a wire at ankle height. The next monster that moves eats dirt — prone, stunned, and embarrassed. (Sets up the party.)
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Steady Hands (Level 1). Fine work under pressure. Dressing game, stitching wounds, tying snares — no shake.
d41: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Grayson Boyd, 41 days. The mantle passes to Stan Kowalski.
d41: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Stan Kowalski, 47 — an exterminator. His hands know different work now: Beast-calm, Lucky Rock.
d41: The village's quarrel was with Grayson — and Grayson is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d41: You knew Grayson — not the office, the person. The fire keeps expecting them, and so do you. That's a heavier kind of stepping up. (+5 trauma)
d41: At the grave, Lorenzo, Lillian, Abdul and 1 more speak for Stan — "Grayson trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d41: The fire knew Stan before the Codex did — his name already carried weight here.
